analogs.name: Gabbro and anorthosite ground — Ellesmere Island

mineralogy.note: Earth: basic plutonic (gabbro, anorthosite) (GLiM). Site: anorthositic highland crust (our reading, not a mapped unit)

similarities: Same rock family: basic plutonic (gabbro, anorthosite), like the anorthositic highland crust
Very dry and bare (117 mm of rain a year, satellite estimate)
The Sun stays low all year at 82° latitude, with long shadows
Ground frozen most of the year (mean surface -21 °C)
differences: Terrain is much flatter than at the site (median slope 1.5° here vs 12.99°)
Mild day-night swing (1.2 K) — far from the Moon's ~300 K
The Moon itself differs from every Earth site: no air at all, 0.17 g gravity and no global magnetic field to block radiation

tests.title: Life-detection limits and drilling for life underground in near-sterile, dry soil
tests.detail: Done before at analog sites: NASA ARADS rover + 2 m drill, Atacama (2016–19); Viking-style tests found almost no organics in Atacama's dry core (Navarro-González et al., *Science* 2003)

analogs.name: Basalt plains — Groot Karasberge

mineralogy.note: Earth: basic volcanic (basalt) (GLiM). Site: lava plains of Amazonis Planitia under a dust and sediment cover (our reading, not a mapped unit)

water_history.note: No global data we could compare

similarities: Slopes match at the same scale (median 0.79° here vs 0.23° at the site)
Same rock family: basic volcanic (basalt), like the lava plains of Amazonis Planitia under a dust and sediment cover
Very dry and bare (64 mm of rain a year, satellite estimate)
differences: Mars itself differs from every Earth site: under 1 % of Earth's air pressure (mostly CO₂), 0.38 g gravity and no global magnetic field to block radiation

tests.title: Rover driving and autonomous navigation, EVA route rehearsal, landing-hazard detection
tests.detail: Done before at analog sites: NASA Desert RATS crewed rover field test, Black Point lava flow, AZ (2010); ESA self-driving rover trial, Erfoud, Morocco (2018); ESA rover prototype "Bridget" with ExoMars prototype instruments, Atacama (2013)
